stories.completionNotes: Took the placeholder-injection path the AC named first: dashboard.html now carries __DEPLOY_VERSION__ and the state server substitutes it in _injectHtml, alongside the existing __SPLASH_TOKEN__ / __DISPLAY_AUTODIM__ / __DISPLAY_CAROUSEL__ seams. No JS reader was added -- one rule owns the chip. THE ONE CALL THE PM SHOULD KNOW ABOUT: the version is read PER REQUEST, not cached at handler construction like the two config placeholders are. deploy-pi.sh restarts eclipse-states-http at step_install_state_server_units (line 1939) but stamps .deploy-version LAST at step_write_deploy_version (line 1955) -- deliberately, per US-354, so a failed restart cannot bump the stamp on a Pi still running old code. A start-time cache would therefore have rendered the PREVIOUS deploy's version on EVERY deploy: green tests, correct-looking code, and the exact stale literal the story exists to delete. Mutation-proved: caching at construction makes the chip read V0.29.23 after V0.29.24 was stamped, and only test_index_readsVersionPerRequest_notCachedAtStartup catches it. Cost is one small JSON read per HTML serve; the kiosk loads the page once. Honest degrade per AC#3: readDeployVersion returns None -- never a guess -- for no-path / absent / unreadable / malformed-JSON / missing / blank / non-string version, and the chip renders the SAME 'V?.?.?' sentinel the splash chip already uses, so one glyph means 'unknown build' on both surfaces. The placeholder is always substituted, so a raw __DEPLOY_VERSION__ can never reach the panel. NO deploy or unit-file change needed: --deploy-version-path defaults to '.deploy-version' (WorkingDirectory-relative, same trick as the existing --config, which ExecStart also does not pass), the service runs as mcornelison from the repo root with no sandboxing directives, and dashboard.html is already vouched in step_install_dashboard_assets so refresh_asset_dir will not prune it. 18 tests, 15 RED-first; the 3 markup guards were mutation-proved after the fact (baking a version literal trips 2, re-baking the dead sentinel trips 3). One test-quality note: the first cut of the no-dead-literal guard matched raw file text and tripped on my own explanatory HTML comment -- it now strips comments and asserts only on renderable markup. Green in-loop: tests/pi/splash + tests/ui + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = exit 0; ruff clean. FILE:// PREVIEW CAVEAT for Iris: an un-substituted preview shows the raw __DEPLOY_VERSION__ text in the chip rather than a pretty sentinel -- the quoted-placeholder trick the two config seams use does not apply to HTML text content. Deliberate: unmistakably 'not substituted', and dev-only. OWED: the on-Pi read of the header chip after deploy (chip must show the real V0.29.xx) -- PM/CIO drill, not codeable.

stories.title: Idle-card clock to 12-hour AM/PM
acceptance: fmtClock (carousel.js:1929) renders 12-hour time with an AM/PM meridiem (mod-12 with 12 for noon/midnight), not getHours() 24-hour
minutes stay zero-padded; no seconds unless already shown
purely a format change -- no data source touched; ruff/lint clean in-loop

stories.goal: As the operator, I want the idle-home clock in 12-hour AM/PM format instead of 24-hour, matching how I read time at a glance.
stories.completionNotes: fmtClock now renders 12-hour AM/PM: mod-12 with 12 restored for midnight/noon, BARE hour ('2:05 PM', never '02:05 PM'), zero-padded minute, no seconds. Pure format change -- no data source, no state file, no emitter touched, and the Date still comes from the caller. THE ONE CALL THE PM SHOULD KNOW ABOUT: I MOVED fmtClock (and its two() padding helper) out of the browser-only `if (typeof document !== 'undefined')` block up into the pure/exported section. That was not a preference -- under 'use strict' an ES6 function declaration inside a block is BLOCK-SCOPED, so fmtClock was structurally unreachable from the api export literal and from every test; hoisting does not rescue it. It was always pure (it formats the Date it is handed; it never reads a clock), so the block comment's 'the pure view logic stays clock-free, so these live in the DOM layer' rationale was true of fmtDate but never of fmtClock. fmtDate + IDLE_DAYS/IDLE_MONTHS deliberately stayed put -- out of scope. There is now exactly ONE clock formatter in carousel.js; the DOM block CALLS it and does not own one, and the source comment there says so to stop a future edit re-declaring a local. 10 tests, all 10 RED first (the DOM one failed on the real rendered value '22:50' -- the actual bug, not a proxy). 3 mutations proved: bare `% 12` without the `|| 12` restore -> midnight+noon+sweep fail; meridiem boundary `h <= 12` -> noon reads AM, caught by 2; RE-SHADOWING the DOM block with the old 24-hour fmtClock -> ALL NINE fmtClock unit tests stay green and ONLY the end-to-end DOM test catches it. That third one is why the story has an end-to-end test at all: it is the exact US-494/US-499/US-502 shape where both halves are individually correct and simply do not agree. Needed a dedicated probe (tests/ui/idle_clock_probe.js) because carousel_probe.js JSON-decodes its arguments and JSON has no Date -- it would hand fmtClock a Number and the formatter would read NaN; the probe builds the Date from local calendar COMPONENTS so the fixture is the clock FACE, not an instant, and the assertions hold in any timezone. Green in-loop: tests/ui + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 580 passed, exit 0 (the 10 new ones verified RUN not skipped, node present); ruff clean. Not run in-loop per TD-059: full pytest + mypy -- but this touches ONE JS function and no Python source, so the regression risk is confined to the UI suite that already ran whole. FLAG FOR THE ON-PI DRILL (layout, not logic): .idle-header is a flex row (wordmark + clock + date, gap 8px) on the 480px design stage, and the clock string grew ~3 glyphs ('22:05' -> '10:05 PM'). I did NOT pre-emptively touch dashboard.css -- the render harness resolves CSS but does not do text metrics, so any tightening would have been a guess at a panel I cannot see. If the header crowds on the real 480x320 panel, that is a one-line CSS follow-up. OWED: the on-Pi read of the idle-card clock at a known time -- PM/CIO drill, not codeable.

stories.title: Battery Health writer: a PRODUCTION drain-event writer (battery_health_log gets new rows again)
acceptance: [CARVED from US-504 per its own conditionalOutcome. Sibling US-504b (verdict producer) is DONE -- it consumes runtime_seconds/timestamps/load_class only and never reads vcell/soc, so this story was NOT blocking it.]

[ROOT -- corrected mechanism] BatteryHealthRecorder.startDrainEvent/endDrainEvent already write start_vcell_v/end_vcell_v/start_soc_pct/end_soc_pct correctly, and scripts/record_drain_test.py populates them. What does not exist is ANY production caller in src/ -- the US-216 auto-open path was retired under US-442/TD-058 and nothing replaced it. Consequence: no running Pi ever writes a battery_health_log row, so the card reads 'unknown' PERMANENTLY, not 'until fresh drains exist'. Build the production writer.

on a real AC->BATTERY transition a drain-event row is opened carrying a REAL start_vcell_v + start_soc_pct read from the MAX17048; on BATTERY->AC (or at cutoff shutdown) it is closed with a real end_vcell_v + end_soc_pct and a real runtime_seconds. Honest-instrument: an unreadable gauge or an uncalibrated SoC register writes NULL, never a guessed number (reuse readCalibratedRegisterSocPct + its cold-start window).

[SEAM] PowerMonitor.onTransition is the existing registration point and PowerMonitor already receives the GPIO6 truth via the US-502 _PowerSourceUiBridge sink (lifecycle.py ~2250). Read the UPS LATE-BOUND, at transition time, not captured at construction (US-501/502/503 all hit the boot-order trap this sprint).

[ORPHAN POLICY -- NEEDS A RULING BEFORE BUILD] US-442 requires a production writer to open+close as a single unit OR guarantee the close on the shutdown path -- but the drain most worth measuring is the one that ENDS in a cutoff shutdown, exactly where a deferred close is most likely to be lost. Options: (A) open-at-loss + close-at-restore-or-shutdown + boot reaper; (B) single INSERT at close, drain held in memory (zero orphans, but a hard crash loses the row entirely); (C) A with the ShutdownSequencer close primary and the reaper as backstop. Ralph recommends (C). See offices/pm/inbox/2026-08-02-from-ralph-us504-carved-504a-writer-504b-producer.md

[LOAD-BEARING TRAP] if a boot reaper is built, it MUST NOT close orphans via endDrainEvent -- that computes runtime_seconds from the timestamp delta, which across a reboot manufactures a runtime spanning the whole downtime, clears the 600s gate, and poisons the verdict median with a fabricated multi-hour 'drain'. The reaper stamps end_timestamp and leaves runtime_seconds NULL so the row can never qualify.

test proves: a simulated AC->BATTERY->AC cycle writes ONE row with real vcell/soc at both ends; an unreadable gauge writes NULL not a guess; the shutdown path closes an open drain; a reaped orphan carries NULL runtime_seconds and does NOT qualify in the US-504b verdict. ruff clean in-loop
does NOT delay, block, or add a failure mode to the ShutdownSequencer -- the drain close is best-effort and can never keep the Pi from powering off (I-038 lesson)

stories.title: Battery Health truthfulness: remove no-source TEMP + HEALTH verdict + last-health-check (Spool spec)
acceptance: [SEQUENCING] wires the BATTERY portion of the consolidated 'Health' card (US-507, landed Sprint 68 / V0.29.23). REMOVE the TEMP tile (MAX17048 has NO temp register) but KEEP the ambient_temp_c column (a future BMP390 baro fills it -- Spool). Keep CELL(volts)+CHARGE(%) as-is (real MAX17048).

[HEALTH VERDICT PRODUCER -- Spool [EXACT] spec] source = battery_health_log (NOT a live MAX17048 spot read -- capacity fade needs runtime-to-cutoff). Qualifying row gate: end_timestamp NOT NULL AND load_class='production' AND runtime_seconds >= [EXACT:600]. RUNTIME_BASELINE_S=[EXACT:727]. States on median of last 3 qualifying drains: good >= [EXACT:80]% baseline (>=582s) | degraded 60-80% (436-582s) | replace < [EXACT:60]% (<436s) | unknown = default (< 3 qualifying in trailing [EXACT:180] days OR any required input NULL). median-of-3 (not last-1: single-drain scatter +-15%).

[LAST-HEALTH-CHECK] = MAX(start_timestamp) over qualifying rows only (a partial/aborted drain is NOT a health check). If last check > [EXACT:90] days old, FORCE verdict to unknown regardless of numbers (stale health data is not health data).

[SEVERITY -- Spool] 🟢 INFORMATIONAL at every state incl 'replace' -- NEVER alarm-red, never owns the screen, never competes with coolant/DTC-STOP on a driving surface (UPS margin is ~12min vs <1min needed = 10x; 'replace' = data-integrity margin thinned, not a car risk).

[HONEST END-STATE] accept the card legitimately reads 'unknown' + last-check '2026-05-16' until fresh qualifying drains exist -- THAT IS THE INSTRUMENT WORKING, not a bug. Test proves the qualifying-gate + median-of-3 + 90-day override + honest-unknown-on-NULL; ruff clean.

validationCriteria.outcome: verdict computed only from qualifying rows via median-of-3 vs the 727s baseline; forces 'unknown' on <3 qualifying / any NULL / >90-day-stale; last-health-check ignores partial drains; renders 🟢 never red; no TEMP tile

conditionalOutcomes: [EXACT:] values (600/727/80/60/180/90) are Spool load-bearing -- flag Spool before any drift
stories.goal: As the operator, I want every battery field on a real source (or absent), so the card is honest -- no 'no source' temp, and a HEALTH verdict grounded in real capacity data rather than a manufactured value or a hardcoded 'unknown'.
stories.completionNotes: US-504 CARVED into US-504a (writer) + this (producer) on the story's own conditionalOutcome -- it grew, and the writer half turned out to be a different, larger animal (see US-504a + the PM note). Every Spool [EXACT] value implemented verbatim, none drifted: 600 gate / 727 baseline / 80-60 bands / 180-day window / 90-day staleness / median-of-3. THE ONE CALL THE PM SHOULD KNOW ABOUT: AC2 called the writer-fix a BLOCKING sub-story on the grounds that 'without this the verdict has nothing to consume' -- that premise is wrong. Spool's own verdict spec reads start_timestamp/end_timestamp/runtime_seconds/load_class and never touches vcell or soc, so the producer was fully buildable without it and is now built + green. That is why this half landed first rather than stalling behind a story that needs two rulings. THE SPEC BUG WORTH THE MOST ATTENTION (filed to Spool 2026-08-02): the qualifying gate (runtime_seconds >= 600) sits entirely ABOVE both sub-good bands (degraded 436-582s, replace <436s). Every row that survives the gate is >=600s therefore >=582s therefore always 'good' -- so through the real pipeline degraded and replace are UNREACHABLE, and a pack that genuinely dies at 500s is filtered out as a 'partial drain' rather than reported as degraded. The verdict silently cannot degrade; it fails safe toward reassurance, the wrong direction for an honest instrument. Implemented VERBATIM anyway (both numbers are [EXACT] Spool values -- flag, never drift), with the bands isolated in a public verdictForMedianRuntime() so the mapping stays fully exercised by tests and only the gate constant has to move when he rules. SECOND CORRECTION for the record: AC2's 'nothing populates start_vcell_v/end_vcell_v/start_soc_pct/end_soc_pct' is right at the data and wrong at the mechanism -- the recorder writes all four correctly and the bench CLI uses them; there is simply ZERO production caller in src/ since US-442/TD-058 retired the auto-open path. So no running Pi writes ANY row, and the card reads 'unknown' permanently rather than 'until fresh drains exist'. That is US-504a. HONEST-INSTRUMENT throughout: unknown is the DEFAULT, never a swallowed failure -- absent DB, unreadable log, unparseable clock, <3 qualifying rows in the trailing 180 days, or a >90-day-stale last check all resolve to unknown, and the staleness override is checked BEFORE the numbers so a stale reading can never paint a confident verdict of any colour. Today that override fires (newest qualifying row 2026-05-16, 78 days) -- the card correctly reads unknown + 2026-05-16, which is the instrument working. ONE VOCABULARY END-TO-END: the old green/attn/low display tiers were a SECOND enum for the same fact (the cross-module enum-identity class that cost the 9-drain saga) and are RETIRED -- battery_health_emitter now re-exports the producer's good/degraded/replace/unknown rather than declaring its own, and carousel.js healthLevel/healthValue speak those words. Severity per Spool: good->ok, degraded AND replace->neutral, unrecognised->unavailable. 'replace' is deliberately NOT red (the UPS carries ~12min against the <1min a clean shutdown needs -- a thinned data-integrity margin is not a car risk) and deliberately NOT ok either (that would claim health the data does not support); neutral is the only tier that neither alarms nor reassures. TEMP tile REMOVED -- the MAX17048 register map has no temperature at all, so the tile rendered 'not captured' on every row ever logged; the ambient_temp_c COLUMN stays for the BMP390. Verdict read is LAZY per emit via getattr, not captured at emitter construction -- the boot-order trap this sprint has now hit in US-501, US-502 and here; it also means a drain recorded while the orchestrator runs reaches the card without a restart. Green in-loop: tests/pi/power + tests/pi/orchestrator + tests/pi/splash/test_battery_health_emitter.py + tests/ui + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 913 passed, exit 0; ruff clean on all 11 touched files (2 import-sort fixes applied). NOT run in-loop per TD-059: full pytest + mypy -- card_state_emitter.py is a base-module touch for the SECOND time this sprint (US-502 was the first), so prioritise the full-suite regression at close. OWED: the seeded-row read of the Health card on the Pi -- PM/CIO drill, not codeable.

[SOURCE-CONFIRM -- grooming gate] confirm the authoritative last-drive source the Pi can read (Pi-local drive_summary / drive boundary event logs) given B-104 made server-side analytics the authority + retired the Pi-side drive_statistics table. The producer reads REAL drive data, never fabricated

stories.goal: As the operator, I want the idle-home card to show my actual last drive instead of 'no recent drive', so I can see recent-drive context at a glance.
stories.completionNotes: PROCESS NOTE FIRST (PM should see this): this story was already implemented, complete and green, but left UNCOMMITTED by the prior iteration -- the identical stall that TD-059 describes and the SECOND consecutive story it has hit (US-504b was recovered the same way). This iteration ran the gate synchronously, verified, and committed (65de58d). Nothing was re-implemented; the work was verified rather than trusted. AC2 SOURCE-CONFIRM (the grooming gate) RESOLVED: the authoritative Pi-local source is drive_summary (US-206), which DriveDetector still writes at every drive start -- it carries the two facts Iris's idle spec asks for (drive identity + when the drive began). B-104 is respected rather than worked around: the producer reads identity + start wall-time ONLY and computes no distance/duration/max/avg, because derived per-drive analytics became the SERVER's authority when US-351 retired the Pi-side drive_statistics table -- re-deriving them here would rebuild exactly what that story deleted. THE ROOT, corrected: the tile did not read 'No recent drive' because a drive was missing, it read it PERMANENTLY. The card had only drive.driveId to read, which is the ACTIVE drive and is null whenever nothing is recording; no producer for the most-recent-COMPLETED drive existed anywhere. The absence was real -- it was the absence of a producer, which is why this could never have self-corrected after a drive. THE DESIGN CALL WORTH KNOWING: the anchor is drive START, not drive end. drive_summary has NO end-of-drive column -- there is no Pi-local record of when a drive finished. Synthesising one (e.g. the newest realtime_data sample) would be a guess dressed as a measurement, and doubly so while capture is down (BL-025), so the fact carried is the one that actually exists. Age is likewise formatted at DISPLAY time from the carried timestamp, never pre-computed at emit: a baked '2 h ago' freezes and ages visibly wrong on a kiosk that emits every few seconds but is read minutes later (same pattern the battery card already uses with lastHealthCheckTs). SIM ROWS ARE FILTERED, not relabelled -- presenting a physics_sim bench run as 'your last drive' would be a fabrication in the only terms the panel has. Consequence to know: on a simulator-only box the tile correctly reads 'No recent drive', which can LOOK like a regression; it is logged at debug distinguishably from 'no rows at all' for exactly that reason. ONE VOCABULARY: agoText extends the EXISTING ageText downward (just now / N min / N h) and hands back to it at a day, so '1 day ago' has exactly one definition on the whole surface -- a second age enum for the same fact is the cross-module enum-identity drift that cost the 9-drain saga. HONEST-INSTRUMENT, per HALF: a drive whose start timestamp is missing/blank/unparseable still renders the drive and admits 'age unknown', because the drive genuinely happened and hiding it would lose a real fact to protect a cosmetic one; a FUTURE stamp reads 'just now' rather than a negative age (the Pi has no RTC battery and boots before NTP settles, so a stamp ahead of now is a routine transient); absent DB, missing table, locked file, empty table or a non-integer drive id all resolve to the honest unknown. lastDrive is ALWAYS a key (null when unknown), never sometimes-absent -- an intermittently-missing key is the shape that lets a renderer quietly fall through to the wrong branch. Boot-order trap avoided for the FOURTH time this sprint (US-501/502/504b were the others): the database is resolved via getattr AT USE TIME, so a drive recorded while the orchestrator runs reaches the card without a service restart. THE TEST THAT MATTERS: the producer's SQL is pinned to the REAL schema -- the test builds the table from production SCHEMA_DRIVE_SUMMARY rather than a hand-rolled fake, so a column-name drift fails LOUDLY instead of silently degrading to a permanent 'unknown' (the exact failure this story exists to fix, and one a fake-DB test would sail through). test_chain_realEmitterToRealRenderer_showsTheRealDrive drives the REAL emitter -> REAL state file -> REAL carousel.js under node, the US-494/499/502/503 two-correct-halves shape. Green in-loop: tests/pi/obdii/test_last_drive_summary.py + tests/pi/orchestrator + tests/pi/splash/test_system_status_last_drive.py + tests/ui/test_carousel_last_drive.py = 196 passed, exit 0, ZERO skips (node present); ruff clean on all 8 files. NOT run in-loop per TD-059: full pytest + mypy -- card_state_emitter.py is a base-module touch for the THIRD time this sprint (US-502, US-504b, this), and system_status_emitter.buildSystemStatusState gained a kwarg, so prioritise the full-suite regression at close. stories.title: BT capture hardening: durable bond + reconnect-transport-reset

validationCriteria.action: simulate a mid-session BT link drop on the Pi (or bench harness)

stories.goal: As the capture service, I want a reconnect after a dropped BT link to reset the transport instead of re-opening a dead tty, so capture recovers cleanly mid-session instead of retrying a stale rfcomm forever.
stories.completionNotes: ROOT, stated precisely because the AC's phrasing understates it: an rfcomm bind is a KERNEL TABLE ENTRY, and it outlives the ACL link. When the dongle drops, /dev/rfcomm0 and the bind record are both still there -- so bindRfcomm's IDEMPOTENT short-circuit ('already bound to the right MAC') hands the retry the same DEAD tty, forever. That is the stale-rfcomm-retry-forever signature. THE ONE THE PM SHOULD KNOW ABOUT: the entry also outlives the PROCESS. A SIGKILLed/crashed predecessor never ran disconnect(), so its binding is still in the kernel table at startup; the new ObdConnection has _boundRfcomm=False, its disconnect (which releases only a binding IT created) skips, bindRfcomm short-circuits on the inherited entry, and the fresh process opens the predecessor's dead tty. So `systemctl restart` did NOT clear this fault -- which is exactly why it read as unfixable in the field. The release therefore had to be keyed on 'the configured port is a MAC', NOT on our own bookkeeping. Pinned by test_connect_staleBindingInheritedFromAPriorProcess_isDroppedNotReused. SECOND DEFECT FOUND WHILE TRACING (not in the AC, and it made the first one unrecoverable): bt_resilience._reactToAdapterUnreachable called _safeDisconnect() -- which RELEASES the binding -- and then waited on ReconnectLoop, whose probe is isRfcommReachable, which REQUIRES the binding to exist. The recovery was waiting for a state its own teardown had just removed, so waitForAdapter could never report success and the reopen never ran. That is why Spool's path ends in a RE-BIND rather than a release: resetTransport() leaves the transport freshly BOUND, which is what makes the probe answer honestly again. AC1 is therefore satisfied at THREE call sites, not one: (a) ObdConnection.reconnect() -> resetTransport(); (b) the per-failed-attempt binding drop inside _performConnect -- the ONLY reset the US-338 post-failure heartbeat ever gets, since it drives connect() and never touches reconnect(); (c) the mixin's ADAPTER_UNREACHABLE path. Missing (b) would have left the heartbeat -- the path that actually runs for hours in the car -- entirely unfixed while every reconnect() test stayed green. AC2 (durable bond): the pair-time half was already shipped (the 2026-07-31 P0 hotfix writes + VERIFIES Paired+Bonded+Trusted). What did not exist was the RUNTIME half -- nothing ever read those flags back. A bond that loses Trusted still reports as paired, but bluez refuses the unattended reconnect, so the symptom is a mystery dead link whose only apparent remedy is a manual re-pair -- which needs the dongle powered, i.e. the engine running, i.e. exactly when you cannot do it. ensureTrusted() repairs trust (a local bluez flag, repairable unattended) and reports an absent bond record honestly with the actual remedy, rather than issuing a trust that cannot help. Best-effort by construction: it can never fail a connect that would otherwise have worked. AC4: no rfkill / hciconfig / nmcli / `power off` anywhere on any new path -- guarded at BOTH the helper level and across the whole recovery, because systemd-rfkill persists radio state at shutdown and that is precisely how the 07-03 soft-block became sticky. eclipse-rfkill-unblock.service stays the standing net; this avoids needing it. AC3 test is real-concurrency and nothing load-bearing is stubbed: real ObdConnection + real bluetooth_helper (bind/release/reset/rfcomm-show parsing AND both layers of the reachability probe) + real BtResilienceMixin + real ReconnectLoop + real connection_log in real SQLite + a real capture THREAD polling while the link drops. Only the OS boundary is faked -- the rfcomm/bluetoothctl CLIs and the python-obd handle -- deliberately at the SUBPROCESS seam, because the defect LIVES INSIDE bindRfcomm; a test that stubs bindRfcomm (as the existing US-221 flap test's _FlappingConnection does) deletes the bug from the test. ONE dongle model (tests/pi/obdii/bt_stack_fake.py) serves both the unit and integration halves. 4 MUTATIONS PROVED: revert the mixin to _safeDisconnect -> 4 integration tests red (and FAST, not hung -- the harness bounds the loop through the same _shutdownEvent seam production uses, so a regression cannot wedge CI); drop the failed-attempt release -> 4 unit tests red; a reconnect() reverted to disconnect()+connect() -> the inherited-binding test red; the AC4 radio guards trip on any rfkill/power-off. TD-072 FILED: 'durable bond' is now defined in two modules (bluetooth_helper for connect-time, pair_obdlink_driver for pair-time). I did NOT consolidate -- the driver is standalone by design (sys.path[0] is scripts/, so a src import needs a __file__ bootstrap) and its failure mode is stranding the car. Mitigation shipped instead: the two are pinned against each other across the whole truth table, so drift fails loudly at test time. Green in-loop: tests/pi/obdii + tests/pi/integration = 795 passed, exit 0; tests/pi/orchestrator + the two root orchestrator-recovery files = 177 passed; ruff clean on all 8 files (1 import-sort autofix). NOT run in-loop per TD-059: full pytest + mypy -- obd_connection.py and bt_resilience.py are both base-module touches on the CAPTURE path, so prioritise the full-suite regression at close. OWED (unchanged by this story): the engine-on validation drive is still the final live acceptance per the story's own conditionalOutcome -- bond-survives-reboot + realtime_data grows. This makes recovery robust; it is not the capture unblock itself (that was the V0.29.22 rfkill hotfix).

stories.goal: As the maintainer, I want to know WHY the BT rfkill soft-block got saved ~07-03, so we can prevent the origin, not just rely on the unblock safety net.
stories.completionNotes: RCA VERDICT: origin UNPROVABLE at this remove; project EXONERATED; mitigation found INSUFFICIENT and hardened. Taking those in order. (1) ORIGIN -- I did NOT name a culprit, deliberately. All three forensic sources are destroyed or out of range: the saved-state file was OVERWRITTEN by the 07-31 recovery (mtime now 2026-07-31 20:26:02, contents 0, and `sudo rm -f /var/lib/systemd/rfkill/*` appears in the Pi's bash_history), the systemd journal retains only back to 2026-07-26 12:39:54 (07-03 is ~3 weeks outside the window), and ~/.bash_history covers only the 07-31 recovery session -- and would never have caught an agent's commands anyway, since `ssh host "cmd"` is non-interactive and does not append to history. Naming a cause on that evidence would have been a guess dressed as a finding, which is the failure mode this project treats as worse than an admitted unknown. (2) THE STRONG FINDING, and the half that IS provable: NO project code or deploy path can produce a soft-block. Exhaustive audit of src/ + scripts/ + deploy/: ZERO `rfkill block`, ZERO `nmcli radio off`, ZERO `hciconfig <dev> down`, ZERO `systemctl stop/disable/mask bluetooth`, ZERO `bluetoothctl power off`. Every radio verb the repo ships points the other way (pair_obdlink.sh:224 `power on`, pair_obdlink_driver.py:300 `_send("power on")`, deploy-pi.sh:838 + the unit `rfkill unblock all`); connect_obdlink.sh's `rfcomm release` is the closest thing to a teardown and it removes a KERNEL BINDING, not radio state. So the surviving explanation is an external/manual action that systemd-rfkill then saved at shutdown exactly as designed -- Atlas's hypothesis, corroborated (NOT proven) by commit ad59561 showing a live-Pi BT 'pairing-saga' debug session dated exactly 2026-07-03. Recorded as suggestive, not conclusive. (3) THE ONE THE PM MUST ACT ON -- AC2 offers a fork: document a prevention OR confirm the unblock service is sufficient mitigation. I could NOT confirm sufficiency, because auditing it turned up a REAL, LIVE-VERIFIED DEFECT. eclipse-rfkill-unblock.service ordered itself After=systemd-rfkill.service -- the PRODUCER half, which its own header calls 'the fix' -- and Before= NOTHING project-owned. Neither rfcomm-bind.service nor eclipse-obd.service declared any relationship to it, so systemd was free to start all three concurrently. Proven on the box, not inferred: `systemctl show` returns Before=multi-user.target shutdown.target only, and on the 2026-07-31 boot rfcomm-bind and eclipse-rfkill-unblock BOTH entered active at 20:25:59 -- the same second. Harmless that boot because the block had already been zeroed by hand; on the one boot where a block IS saved it is a coin flip, and the losing side binds /dev/rfcomm0 against a dark adapter while EVERY unit still reads `active` -- the exact 'green-looking unit on a dark adapter' the unit's header set out to prevent. WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT (sixth sighting this sprint of the US-494/499/502/503/505 two-correct-halves shape): the pre-existing test_unitManifest_ordersTheUnblockBeforeTheRfcommBind asserted the ordering against unit_manifest.START_ORDER, a hand-ordered PYTHON TUPLE. unit_manifest's own header states its ordering is 'grounded in the units' own declarations, NOT invented' and then lists the declarations it relies on -- none of which mention the unblock unit. So that was the single entry in the tuple with nothing behind it. The manifest is not decorative (obdctl sequences its own start/stop by it) but it CANNOT order boot, and boot is exactly when a restored block bites. FIX: Before=rfcomm-bind.service eclipse-obd.service. `Before=` and deliberately NOT `Wants=` -- it orders those consumers if they are already in the boot transaction and must never pull them in; no cycle (the unblock is After=bluetooth.service and neither consumer is an ancestor). NO deploy-script change needed: step_install_rfkill_unblock is cmp -s-guarded, so the changed unit installs + daemon-reloads on the next routine deploy -- BUT THE RACE IS STILL LIVE ON THE PI UNTIL THAT DEPLOY RUNS. PREVENTION SHIPPED: tests/deploy/test_no_radio_disable_in_project.py, a repo-wide static guard that turns finding (2) from a point-in-time audit into a standing invariant. US-512 already guards this at RUNTIME but only for two helpers and only for commands they emit -- a new script or deploy step is invisible to it. Guard design notes: patterns match ARGV LISTS as well as shell strings, because its own self-test caught on the FIRST run that a whitespace-only separator sees every `sudo rfkill block` and misses every `subprocess.run(["rfkill","block"])` -- which is the form bluetooth_helper actually uses; `\bblock\b` after a token separator so `rfkill unblock all` is not condemned (otherwise the guard flags the FIX for the outage it prevents -- pinned by an explicit permit-list test over all 8 restorative forms); whole-line # comments stripped per US-501's lesson, since bluetooth_helper.py and obd_connection.py both DOCUMENT these forbidden commands and a raw-text scanner would flag the prose explaining the rule; tests/ deliberately not scanned because US-512's guards assert on these strings literally; greppable `radio-guard-exempt` escape hatch per the explicit-hatch-over-drift rule. MUTATION-PROVED end-to-end, not just as regex: a real violating .sh dropped into scripts/ trips test_noShippedFileDisablesARadio with a precise file:line message (probe removed). The 4 new ordering tests were RED-first for the right reason before the unit changed. ONE DISCRIMINATOR DELIBERATELY LEFT UNTESTED, flagged to PM: whether `bluetoothctl power off` can itself produce a SAVED block. Settling it means disabling a radio on the car Pi and rebooting; I declined under the standing 'never disable a radio on the Pi remotely' rule (the 2026-07-19 nmcli radio wifi off stranding), with an owed engine-on drive on the box. Safe path is a bench Pi or the car Pi with the CIO present, and it changes NO conclusion above -- the project does not issue that command either way. ALSO FLAGGED TO PM (box-config, not mine to change): the Pi's ~1-week journal retention is the single reason this RCA cannot close harder; a SystemMaxUse=/MaxRetentionSec= bump would make the next slow-burn fault answerable. Green in-loop: tests/deploy + tests/pi/ops = exit 0 (374 existing + 25 new pass, zero skips); ruff clean on both touched test files. NOT run in-loop per TD-059: full pytest + mypy -- but this story touches ONE systemd unit and TWO test files and no Python source, so regression risk is confined to the deploy suite that already ran whole. OWED: nothing codeable. The validationCriteria's 'test whether the identified trigger reproduces the saved-block' is NOT satisfiable -- no trigger was identified to reproduce, and the evidence needed to identify one no longer exists; that is the honest finding, not a skipped step.
